messages:
meera: Quick question — when a proxy service calls downstream Redwood APIs on behalf of multiple projects, how should we represent origin so quotas, billing, and console traces all line up?

meera: current hack is `X-Forwarded-Project: <proj>` + proxy API key, but telemetry is messy and billing shows proxy owner, not end project.

dan: ugh yeah saw that in the last telemetry spike. proxy owners get the cost, which is wrong.

alex: two obvious options: 1) token exchange / short-lived impersonation tokens (subject = end-project), or 2) an origin claim inside the JWT signed by proxy (we verify signature).

priya: exchange solves billing/quotas cleanly but needs STS + perf hit. origin-claim + signature is lower latency but requires trust model + console UX to show "effective project" vs "request principal".

meera: can we do a hybrid? proxy can mint an ephemeral token for heavy callers and attach `x-origin-project` when latency matters.

sam: hybrid makes sense. for bursty paths we can skip exchange if we mark requests as non-billable until reconciled, but that's risky.

alex: also consider sticky routing — route by origin claim to the right quota shard without swapping commit ownership. gives correct throttling but billing attribution still needs an identity to charge.

infra-bot: note: last deploy added `request.origin_project` field to traces but UI is off by one for proxied calls. (linked: https://console/internal/traces/PROXY-123)

priya: UX ask: Console needs a clear column: "Caller" (token owner) + "Effective Project/Org" (origin/impersonation). That way support can see who to ping and who bears cost.

dan: implementation question — where do we record this? request context? a new `origin_project_id` column in events table? that would require migrating long-term metrics.

meera: prefer minimal schema change: piggyback on `request.attributes` JSON blob for now, with a derived column for queries. then we can backfill to a native column later.

alex: security note: if we accept `x-origin-project` from untrusted proxies, attackers could spoof project to dodge quotas. must require either signed header (HMAC) or token exchange.

priya: +1. if we go signed header route, define verification keys: proxies get signing keys via KMS and we publish their public keys to the authz service. easy to verify in the runtime.

sam: perf numbers: token exchange adds ~30-50ms on cold but can be cached per connection; HMAC verification is ~1-2ms. tradeoffs clear.

meera: decision proposal: default = signed origin header (HMAC) for low-latency paths, token exchange/impersonation for high-trust/billing-critical flows. console shows both principal + effective project. add telemetry flag `origin_verification_method`.

dan: +1 but we need a migration plan for existing proxies. rollout plan?

meera: rollout: 1) new proxies adopt signed headers; 2) runtime starts honoring `origin_project` in telemetry (opt-in); 3) console shows effective project column behind a feature flag; 4) enforce only for billing-critical endpoints after 90d.

alex: add a canary: honor signed header only for a subset of shards first, and emit a metric `auth.origin_verification.failures`.

infra-bot: metric `auth.origin_verification.failures` created on 1745558142.

priya: small API note for SDKs: add helper to produce signed origin header: `signOriginHeader(proxy_key, project_id, expires_at)` with HMAC-SHA256. include example in docs.

meera: docs + SDKs is critical. without it teams will hack around the header.

sam: ok will add to SDK backlog. tagging @meera for acceptance criteria. :thumbsup: 

meera: thanks — i'll draft the acceptance checklist: HMAC format, verification code, metrics, console column, migration schedule. I'll post in this thread when ready.

alex: cool, ping infra when you have the draft.

priya: also file a short security review for the key distribution plan.

meera: will do.

sam: AWOL note: if anyone sees anomalies in billing during rollout, please loop billing@redwood and ops.

meera: good call. closing for now — follow-up doc incoming.
